_meta.description: Hand-labelled ground truth for 19 real scanned CY-*.pdf documents under 00_gelen_kaynaklar/cevap_yazisi/, stratified over single- and multi-page scans and over the corpus's distinct letterhead templates (MSB, Ticaret, Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı, Sanayi ve Teknoloji, Hazine ve Maliye, TBMM). Page 1 was read visually for each document; only page 1 is labelled, matching the header fields this corpus's RYUEHY compliance check reads. The 4 documents added after the initial 15 (CY-006, CY-023, CY-028, CY-034) were added specifically to test a signature-detection finding: the initial 15-document sample showed 0% signature recall, traced to two compounding bugs in marks.py (the stamp shape check intercepting real signatures before the signature check ever ran, and _SIGNATURE_ZONE_START_FRACTION excluding signatures that sit mid-page rather than literally the bottom third on these short-bodied letters) -- these 4 were chosen from documents the position-based heuristic flagged as signature-shaped but outside the original sample, specifically to check whether that positional signal was reliable or coincidental. All 4 turned out to be genuine wet signatures, on the same letterhead templates (Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı, Millî Savunma Bakanlığı, TBMM Kanunlar ve Kararlar Başkanlığı) as documents already confirmed signed in the original 15 -- strong evidence the corpus's signature placement is template-driven and the position signal generalises, not an artifact of the original sample.
_meta.clean_text_convention: Each entry's 'clean_text' is a faithful transcription of page 1's header/addressee/reference/closing/signature-block lines (body paragraphs are shortened -- their exact wording never affects which fields the deterministic parser recovers). Expected fields are meant to be derived by running 'clean_text' through the same app.ai.compliance.field_parser.parse_labelled_fields() the OCR benchmark scores against, exactly mirroring how scripts/evaluate_ocr_fields.py derives its own ground truth from datasets/sample/evrak_*.txt ('Ground truth is the parse of the source text, not the JSON annotation'). A field the parser cannot recover even from this clean transcript (e.g. muhatap on CY-010, where the addressee is a named MP rather than a dative-suffixed institution; gonderen_kurum on CY-010, whose TBMM letterhead carries no 'T.C.' line) is left absent from the parse by construction -- that is a parser-architecture limit, not an OCR-quality question, so it must not be scored against any engine.
_meta.mark_labels: has_signature / has_stamp / has_handwriting are visual judgements from the page image, independent of clean_text. has_signature means a signature-shaped ink mark is visible over the printed name (regardless of whether the document is legally e-imza-authenticated -- several documents carry both a 'Bu belge güvenli elektronik imza ile imzalanmıştır' notice AND a visible signature-style scrawl rendered into the PDF). has_stamp is reserved for a genuine applied ink chop/mühür distinct from the printed T.C./ministry letterhead crest -- the letterhead crest itself is NOT counted as a stamp here, since marks.py's own calibration notes (see scripts/evaluate_marks.py and the plan history) found its stamp detections are largely letterhead-emblem shaped, and conflating the two would make it impossible to tell a real detector improvement from a definitional one.
_meta.handwritten_digit_uncertainty: Several 'sayı' values include a handwritten numeric suffix appended by hand next to a printed reference prefix (MSB, Ticaret Bakanlığı, Hazine ve Maliye templates). Cursive digits are inherently ambiguous to a human reader too; these are best-effort transcriptions, not certified exact. This uncertainty is itself informative for the benchmark -- it is exactly the content vision models are being compared on.
_meta.labelled_by: manual visual reading of each PDF's page 1
